Friday-announced expanded PepsiCo transaction framed as a strategic step change: Celsius becomes PepsiCo's energy category captain.
Deal brings Alani Nu into the PepsiCo distribution system, adds Rockstar Energy (~$250M revenue), $585M PepsiCo equity investment and a second Board seat.
Captaincy gives Celsius control of national planograms across PepsiCo Energy - choosing which SKUs go where ('put the fast cars on the track').
Portfolio positioned as 'total/modern energy': Celsius (fitness, 50-50 gender), Alani Nu (female-focused), Rockstar (traditional, male 25-35), Celsius Essentials (16-oz performance).
Rockstar explicitly framed as a turnaround ('one step back'): Phase 1 SKU optimization, then stabilization, then growth - no fixed blueprint, but it has a place.
No cannibalization observed - Alani Nu and Celsius both growing despite earlier concern given Celsius's 50-50 gender base.
Energy category robust (~17-18% trailing 4-wk growth) vs more challenged other categories and restaurant industry.
Consumers pivoting from cold coffee into energy seeking value; energy retains value while broad beverage pricing has been taken.
Channel shift: large format / 12-packs / variety packs gaining mix vs the historical >60% impulse-purchase profile.
Management reiterated the deal does NOT change prior margin/EBITDA outlook, yet framed it as the deal that enables historically targeted margin profiles.
Single distribution system (vs two) avoids significant operating expense; Orbit model (procure/produce/sell within an orbit) enhances supply chain efficiency.
Alani Nu transition managed with weekly stakeholder reviews, a project manager, and a green/yellow/red stop-light process; key-accounts team ~3x larger than 2022.
Rockstar revitalization to focus on music and extreme sports; Pacific Northwest its biggest market and primary learning ground.
Catalysts: Alani Nu distribution transition (Dec 1), Rockstar close + SKU optimization, NACS convenience show for 2026 planograms, 2026 four-brand go-to-market.
Intra-quarter (Q3) trends described as looking good; tone upbeat, strategic and execution-focused.
What does the PepsiCo agreement really mean for Celsius's long-term strategy?

Tying into a strategic distribution partner is decisive in the impulse-driven energy category (compared to Red Bull's network and Monster/Coca-Cola); captaincy enables high-level commercial planning, priority periods and planograms; Celsius can pick which SKUs go where nationally.
What changes in terms of visibility - does the captaincy improve access to the full data picture, and how does the retailer role change?

Two pieces: captaincy/planograms within PepsiCo and the retail segment; company maintains call points and builds key-accounts team; now controls planograms across PepsiCo independents, foodservice, colleges, restaurants - optimizing SKU mix locally by demographics (Marriott example).
Servicing the full spectrum of energy consumers
How does having Celsius, Alani Nu and Rockstar under one roof change the ability to serve the full energy-consumer spectrum?

Gives a total/modern energy approach with distinct brands - Celsius (fitness, 50-50), Alani Nu (female, approachable), Rockstar (traditional, ~50% of segment, male 25-35); each brand has its own personality; Rockstar back to core with SKU optimization.
Read on the US consumer backdrop lately.

Energy category robust (~17-18% trailing 4-wk growth) vs more challenged other categories; Red Bull, Monster, Alani Nu, Celsius all growing; economically challenged consumers pivoting from cold coffee into energy; large format/variety packs gaining mix.
Is there a relative value proposition driving consumers from coffee-shop coffee toward energy?

Confirmed a multi-year transition from coffee drinkers into energy; much coffee-house consumption now cold rather than hot, making the shift to canned energy easier and potentially further aiding category growth.
Alani Nu distribution opportunity vs Celsius transition
Opportunities for Alani Nu as it transitions into PepsiCo's US/Canada distribution, and comparison to the Celsius transition.

PepsiCo network brings Alani Nu to more places - biggest opportunities in convenience, small format, restaurants, foodservice, hospitals, universities; Alani Nu's convenience ACV/SKU level similar to pre-PepsiCo Celsius; intra-Q3 numbers looking good; feared cannibalization did not materialize.
What food pairs best with Alani Nu?

Depends on flavor - peach pairs well, cotton candy less so, Fieldly cited Cherry Slush; Celsius's soda-like flavors probably pair better across the board (lighthearted exchange, limited investment substance).
Detail on plans to stabilize and modernize Rockstar and its role in the portfolio, noting it sounds like one step back before moving forward.

Goal to maximize Rockstar value: Phase 1 portfolio/SKU optimization focusing on the true core with talented incoming people and a laser go-to-market; restructured to manage a portfolio; no blueprint but it has a place; focus on music and extreme sports leveraging brand heritage (once #3 energy drink).
Rockstar is a turnaround requiring a different mentality - does the team have that turnaround capability?

Celsius itself was a turnaround when Fieldly started (getting kicked out of every retailer); now a ~20% portfolio share; far greater capabilities today, disciplined; revitalizing brands very difficult but optimistic; portfolio approach gives holding power and pricing/promo levers; large-format share upwards of 25%.
Is the Pacific Northwest the key market to focus on for Rockstar given its strength there?

Pacific Northwest is Rockstar's biggest market and primary learning ground; bring on the team that knows it, leverage Celsius resources, then scale; emphasized daily consumption and daily users as the name of the game, built on brand DNA.
PepsiCo confidence & financial impact of the deal
How to think about PepsiCo's additional $585M equity investment and second board seat re confidence in Celsius, and the expected financial impact of the deal.

Investment shows PepsiCo highly confident in Celsius's capabilities (partnership since 2022); building specialized convenience/foodservice/mass teams; Rockstar ~$250M incremental revenue; prior PepsiCo incentive program enhanced; reiterated not changing future outlook - deal doesn't drastically change margin/EBITDA outlook.
Why wouldn't the deal be an outright accelerator rather than just an enabler?

Deal would help accelerate top-line growth but would not ascribe a number; bringing Alani Nu into PepsiCo accelerates its ramp; running one system avoids significant operating expense and provides the opportunity to reach historically targeted gross-margin/EBITDA profiles; Orbit model supports EPS accretion.
Alani Nu transition from ABI to PepsiCo / disruption management
How is the company managing the transition of Alani Nu away from ABI distributors into PepsiCo, and what steps minimize disruption?

Transition anticipated first of December; done before with Celsius; processes, checkpoints, weekly stakeholder reviews, project manager, green/yellow/red stop-light process; ~80% of distribution moving on roughly the same timeline; transitions difficult (scanning issues) but key-accounts team ~3x larger than 2022.
Learnings from prior route-to-market noise (~12 months ago) being brought into these transitions.

Celsius transition went well with no large 2022 impact; ABI distributors were phenomenal and supportive; there are distributor buyouts associated with the transactions; company has been open and transparent; some distributors have reconciliation challenges, distributors expected to receive sizable buyouts.
With Celsius as PepsiCo's energy captain, what does success look like over the next two to three years?

Deal a step change tying into a strategic partner, following the proven Monster/Coca-Cola model; in 2-3 years expects an amazing portfolio with a meaningful energy-category position; from ~20% share today keep building Celsius, Alani Nu, Rockstar and Celsius Essentials, leveraging PepsiCo distribution fully.
